whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Communications Cloud Accredited Professional exam for?

personas.label: Telecom implementers
personas.description: You build Communications Cloud for mobile, broadband or media providers and want to prove you know the industry setup.

personas.label: Consultants and admins
personas.description: You work on the product catalog, quoting or ordering side of a telecom project.

personas.label: Career builders
personas.description: You know core Salesforce and want to specialise in the communications industry.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Communications Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The pass mark is low, but the exam isn't easy. Communications Cloud has its own catalog, quoting and ordering tools that work very differently from standard Salesforce products and orders.
bullets: Industry tools. Enterprise Product Catalog, Industries CPQ, Industries Order Management and OmniStudio.
Telecom processes. Move, add, change and disconnect orders, contracts and assets come up often.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: People who have configured offers in the product catalog and pushed an order through decomposition do best. Before you book. Aim for 75% or more on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Communications Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe a telecom task, such as building a bundle, pricing an offer or changing a customer's existing service, and ask which tool or setting handles it.
bestWayToPass: Learn the catalog building blocks: Products, attributes, offers, bundles, promotions and price lists.
Understand rules: Eligibility, compatibility and context rules decide who can buy what and in which combinations.
Follow an order through Industries Order Management: Decomposition into technical orders, then orchestration of fulfilment steps.
Know OmniStudio basics: OmniScripts, FlexCards, Integration Procedures and Data Mappers.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you set up Communications Cloud for telecom and media providers: the product catalog, quoting, ordering and fulfilment, contracts and assets, and the OmniStudio tools. The exam is 55 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 56% pass mark, weighted towards Planning and Design (60%) and Discovery (24%).

keyConcepts.h2: Communications Cloud AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Product Catalog & Offer Management
blocks.body: The **Enterprise Product Catalog (EPC)** holds everything the provider sells. **Products** describe a service or device. **Attributes** describe options like speed or colour. **Offers** are what customers can actually buy, often **bundles** of several products, such as broadband plus TV. **Promotions** add time-limited discounts. **Price lists** hold prices and can differ by channel or market. Building offers from reusable products means a change to one product, like a new router, flows to every offer that uses it.

blocks.heading: Industries CPQ for Telco
blocks.body: **Industries CPQ** uses a cart. Agents or customers add offers, choose attributes and see the price straight away. **Rules** keep the cart valid: **eligibility** rules decide whether a customer can see an offer, for example by region, and **compatibility** rules stop invalid combinations, such as two broadband plans on one line. **Context rules** use details about the customer or location to change what is shown. The same cart logic can be used in agent screens and in **Digital Commerce** for online channels, through APIs.

blocks.heading: Order Management & Orchestration
blocks.body: When an order is submitted, **Industries Order Management** breaks the commercial order into the technical pieces needed to deliver it. This is called **decomposition**. An **orchestration plan** then runs the steps in the right order, such as reserve a number, ship a router, then activate the line, calling outside systems as needed. If a step fails, the plan can retry, wait or alert someone. Customers see one order, while the back office handles many technical tasks.

blocks.heading: Contract & Subscription Lifecycle
blocks.body: Once an order is fulfilled, the services become **assets** on the customer's account. Later changes are known as **MACD**: move, add, change and disconnect. For example, upgrading a broadband speed is a change to an existing asset, not a brand-new order. **Contracts** record terms like length and early-exit fees, and can be renewed. Keeping assets accurate is important because every future change starts from them.

blocks.heading: Partner Ecosystem & Channel Management
blocks.body: Providers often sell through retail shops, partners and online. Experience Cloud sites can give partners their own sales tools, using the same catalog and cart as internal agents, with partner-specific price lists or offers. **OmniStudio** tools power many of these screens: **OmniScripts** guide users through steps, **FlexCards** show key customer details at a glance, **Integration Procedures** fetch data from several systems in one call, and **Data Mappers** read, change and save data.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Communications Cloud Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions name a telecom task and ask which tool handles it. Learn where each job lives: catalog, cart, order management or assets.

blocks.heading: Communications Cloud Data Model
blocks.body: Accounts are often split into consumer, billing and service accounts. Assets on the service account show what the customer has.

blocks.heading: Industries CPQ for Telecom
blocks.body: The cart applies eligibility and compatibility rules. If an offer doesn't appear, check eligibility first.

blocks.heading: Order Management for CSPs
blocks.body: Decomposition turns a commercial order into technical orders. Orchestration runs the fulfilment steps.

blocks.heading: Customer 360 for Telecom
blocks.body: FlexCards give agents a quick view of the customer's services, bills and open orders.

blocks.heading: OmniStudio in Communications Cloud
blocks.body: OmniScripts for guided steps, Integration Procedures for server-side data calls, Data Mappers for reading and writing data.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Communications Cloud:

sampleQuestions.question: A provider wants to sell broadband, a router and TV together as one package at a special price. How should this be set up in the catalog?
options: As a price list with one product
As a bundle offer of the three products
As a contract with three line items only
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bundles let you sell several products together as one offer, with their own pricing.
whyWrong: A price list holds prices. It doesn't group products into a package.
A contract records terms after the sale. It isn't how products are packaged.
Three orders lose the package price and are harder for customers.

sampleQuestions.question: A new fibre plan should only be offered to customers in areas where fibre is available. What should be used?
options: A product price list on the catalogue
An eligibility rule for the offer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Eligibility rules decide whether a customer can see an offer, for example based on location.
whyWrong: Compatibility rules stop invalid combinations in the cart, not who can see an offer.
A price list sets prices, not availability.
A promotion gives a discount, it doesn't limit availability.

sampleQuestions.question: Customers must not be able to add two broadband plans to the same line. What enforces this?
options: An eligibility rule for the offer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Compatibility rules stop combinations that don't make sense in the cart.
whyWrong: A Data Mapper moves data, it doesn't validate the cart.
A FlexCard displays information.
Eligibility controls who sees an offer, not combinations.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer orders broadband. The back office needs to reserve a port, ship a router and activate the line. What breaks the order into these technical steps?
options: A product price list on the catalogue
An eligibility rule for the offer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Decomposition turns the commercial order into the technical orders needed for fulfilment.
whyWrong: Promotions affect price.
Price lists hold prices.
Eligibility rules affect which offers show.

sampleQuestions.question: After decomposition, which feature runs the fulfilment steps in the right order and calls outside systems?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Orchestration plans run fulfilment tasks in sequence, handle dependencies and call outside systems.
whyWrong: Eligibility rules control what can be sold.
Contracts record terms.
FlexCards show data to users.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer wants to upgrade their existing broadband from 100 Mbps to 500 Mbps. How should this be handled?
options: As an entirely brand-new order for the broadband product
As a change order on the existing asset
sampleQuestions.explanation: Upgrades are changes (the C in MACD) to an existing asset, which keeps history and avoids duplicate services.
whyWrong: A new order would create a second broadband service.
The price list sets prices for everyone.
Deleting the asset loses history and breaks billing.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool guides a service agent step by step through a complex process, such as moving a customer to a new address?
options: A product price list on the catalogue
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScripts are guided, step-by-step processes for users.
whyWrong: Compatibility rules check the cart.
Price lists hold prices.
Data Mappers read and write data, they don't guide users.

sampleQuestions.question: Agents need to see a customer's services, last bill and open orders at a glance on one screen. What fits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: FlexCards show key information in a compact, actionable card.
whyWrong: Orchestration runs fulfilment steps.
Promotions are discounts.
Decomposition breaks down orders.

sampleQuestions.question: A screen needs data from billing, network inventory and Salesforce in one fast server-side call. What should be used?
options: A FlexCard used on its own
A product price list on the catalogue
sampleQuestions.explanation: Integration Procedures run several data actions on the server in one call, which keeps screens fast.
whyWrong: A FlexCard displays data, but it needs a data source like an Integration Procedure.
Promotions are discounts.
Price lists hold prices.

sampleQuestions.question: A new router model replaces the old one in 20 different offers. What is the benefit of building offers from reusable products?
options: Each one of the offers must be edited by hand
One update to the router reaches every offer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reusable products mean a change in one place flows to every offer that includes it.
whyWrong: Existing customers don't need to reorder.
The point of reuse is to avoid editing every offer.
Offers keep working with the updated product.

sampleQuestions.question: A three-month 20% discount for new customers should be added to a mobile plan. What should be used?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Promotions add time-limited discounts or changes to offers.
whyWrong: A new product isn't needed for a discount.
Compatibility rules check combinations.
Orchestration runs fulfilment.

sampleQuestions.question: Why is it important to keep customer assets accurate in Communications Cloud?
options: The assets end up controlling the website's theme
Assets are only used for reports
Moves, changes and disconnects start from assets
sampleQuestions.explanation: MACD orders change existing assets. If the assets are wrong, every later change is wrong too.
whyWrong: Assets don't control the website.
Prices come from price lists.
They are used in orders, not just reports.

sampleQuestions.question: A partner shop should sell from the same catalog as internal agents, but with its own prices. What should be set up?
options: A copy of the whole catalog for the partner
Manual price changes on each order
A separate org for the partner
sampleQuestions.explanation: Price lists can differ by channel, so partners use the same catalog with their own prices.
whyWrong: Copying the catalog doubles the upkeep.
Manual changes are slow and error-prone.
A separate org is far more than needed.

sampleQuestions.question: A fulfilment step fails because the network activation system is down. What should the orchestration plan do?
options: Retry or pause the step and alert someone
Simply mark the whole of the order as complete
sampleQuestions.explanation: Orchestration can retry, wait or raise an alert on failed steps, so the order can continue once the problem is fixed.
whyWrong: Marking it complete would leave the customer without service.
Deleting loses the sale.
A new order duplicates work.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool should read data from Salesforce, transform it and save it back as part of an OmniScript?
options: A product price list on the catalogue
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Mappers (formerly DataRaptors) read, transform and save data for OmniStudio tools.
whyWrong: Promotions are discounts.
Price lists hold prices.
FlexCards display data.
